pages.text: Daisy is a dolphin in the ocean. She is a mammal, like people, so she breathes air and feeds her baby milk.
Daisy swims with her family group called a pod. Pods help dolphins stay safe and find food together.
Daisy must breathe air. She swims up to the surface and takes a quick breath through her blowhole.
Underwater, Daisy makes clicking sounds. The clicks bounce back as echoes and tell her what is nearby.
This echo-finding is called echolocation. Daisy can find fish even when the water looks dark or cloudy.
Daisy also whistles to talk. Dolphins use clicks and whistles to communicate with friends and family.
Daisy’s tail flukes move up and down to swim. Her fins help her steer left, right, and around rocks.
Daisy plays by jumping and splashing. Playing helps dolphins learn, practice skills, and stay strong.
Daisy remembers: breathe at the surface, swim with the pod, and use echoes to find food safely.
At the end of the day, Daisy rests and floats quietly. Her pod stays close in the calm ocean.
